entities.summary:
The National Rally (Rassemblement National, formerly Front National) is France's major far-right political party, founded in 1972 by Jean-Marie Le Pen, which has transformed from a fringe extremist movement to a mainstream force winning 30%+ of French votes and narrowly missing the French presidency multiple times. Marine Le Pen's rebranding from Front National to Rassemblement National in 2018 and her 2022 presidential runoff (receiving 41.45% against Macron) represent the most dramatic normalization of far-right politics in post-war Western Europe.

Jean-Marie Le Pen, a paratrooper veteran of Indochina and Algeria, founded the Front National as an alliance of Vichy nostalgics, Catholic traditionalists, and anti-immigrant nationalists. The FN's breakthrough came in 1984 European elections (10.9%) and Le Pen's 2002 presidential runoff against Jacques Chirac — which shocked France and Europe by reaching the second round, creating a 'republican front' that gave Chirac 82% in the runoff.

Marine Le Pen expelled her father from the party in 2015, removing Holocaust minimization and Vichy nostalgia from the party's image while maintaining anti-immigration and euro-skeptic positions. Jordan Bardella's 2024 European election victory (31.4%) and the subsequent dissolution of the National Assembly by Macron — who was trying to force a resolution — led to RN winning the most seats in the 2024 legislative election, threatening a cohabitation government under Bardella that was ultimately avoided by a left-wing coalition.
